## ARCHIE WATER SATURATIONS: $S_W$ AND $S_{XO}$
Water saturation ($S_w$) of a reservoir's uninvaded zone is calculated by the Archie (1942) formula:
$$ S_w = \left( \frac{a \times R_w}{R_t \times \phi^m} \right)^{\frac{1}{n}} \tag{7.1} $$

Saturation crossplots, also called resistivity-porosity crossplots (or specifically, Pickett plots and Hingle plots) are similar to the porosity crossplots discussed
## Pickett Crossplot Method
The Pickett plot (Pickett, 1966, 1973) is one of the simplest and most effective crossplot methods in use. This technique estimates water saturation and can also
- formation water resistivity ($R_w$) - cementation factor ($m$) - matrix parameters for sonic and density logs ($\Delta t_{ma}$ and $\rho_{ma}$)
The Pickett method is based on the observation that true resistivity ($R_t$) is a function of porosity ($\phi$), water saturation ($S_w$), and cementation exponent
$$R_t = \frac{a \times R_o}{\phi^m \times S_w^n} \tag{7.23}$$
